title: Inequality Constraints Separating the E-NE Model from the Nested Markov Model in Bow-Free Graphs
banked_reason: Sound subfield result, but arbitrary distance-two forests and disconnected endpoints remain unclassified, so the graph-readable theorem is sufficient rather than necessary-and-sufficient; the pointwise membership system is not a graph-uniform facet description.
gap_reasons: It does not deliver the advertised broader forest frontier: arbitrary distance-two forests and disconnected arrow endpoints remain unclassified, so the graph-readable result is a sufficient strictness regime rather than a necessary-and-sufficient characterization.
The displayed inequality is not shown to be facet-defining or complete, and the membership system depends on the supplied law rather than yielding a graph-uniform polytope or inequality description.

The framing accurately discloses these limitations, but their combination keeps the contribution specialized and limits its projected leading-econometrics-journal score despite clearing the field-contribution floor.
proof_attempt_summary: The discovery phase established a sound vertex-minimal positive E/NE-versus-NM separator, equality through three vertices, a distance-at-least-three one-arrow forest separation theorem, a star equality regime, and an exact pointwise response-table LP. Math, rubric, and citation checks passed, but the field-level promise collapsed because distance-two and disconnected-endpoint forests remain unclassified and the inequality/membership results are not complete or graph-uniform. A future re-raise should reuse these proofs and attack that missing necessary-and-sufficient frontier rather than re-derive the four-node witness.
tldr: This note proves that E/NE and nested Markov coincide for every binary bow-free graph on at most three vertices; gives an exact positive separating inequality and nested-but-not-E/NE law for \(A\leftrightarrow B\leftrightarrow C\leftrightarrow D, A\to D\); extends the obstruction to one-arrow bidirected forests whose directed endpoints have distance at least three, with violation approaching the universal \(1/2\) limit; proves a complementary star equality regime; and establishes an exact finite response-table membership procedure. These results separate marginal-Markov error semantics from both equality-only nested Markov models and stronger canonical latent-DAG semantics. A necessary-and-sufficient criterion for distance-two and disconnected-endpoint one-arrow forests remains open.
gap: Zhao's E/NE model is proposed as a default ADMG semantics and is known to lie inside NM, but its additional inequalities are essentially undeveloped beyond inherited examples such as IV. The nearest graphical inequality classifications concern canonical latent-DAG or mDAG margins, whose independent latent-source factorization is stronger than E/NE's setwise Markov condition on errors.
fill: Establish a vertex-minimal separator, a reusable distance-based strictness theorem, a nontrivial equality family, and an exact membership equivalence; leave only sharply identified distance-two and disconnected-endpoint forest classes as an explicit open frontier.
